feedback.problem:
Express the Maclaurin series expansion for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+{x}^{2}),$ given by

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+{x}^{2})={x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{6}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{8}+⋯
$$

using sigma notation.
feedback.worked_solution:
The first four terms of the series are

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & ={x}^{2} \\ {a}_{2} & =-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{6} \\ {a}_{3} & =-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we can express these terms using a common format, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =\frac{(-1)^{1+1}{x}^{2\cdot 1}}{1} \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{(-1)^{2+1}{x}^{2\cdot 2}}{2} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{(-1)^{3+1}{x}^{2\cdot 3}}{3} \\ {a}_{4} & =\frac{(-1)^{4+1}{x}^{2\cdot 4}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We deduce that the general formula for the $n$th term is

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{x}^{2n}}{n}\,.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+{x}^{2})={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{x}^{2n}}{n}.
$$
